description: One-line plain-English summaries of what happens in each reading, keyed by verse range ('<Book> <start>-<end>') rather than by aliyah, so that ranges shared between an ordinary parsha, its combined (double) form, a maftir and a chag reading resolve to the same entry instead of being written several times. Hand-written, then machine-checked: tools/check_summaries.mjs verifies that every proper name mentioned in a summary actually appears in the Hebrew of that verse range, which catches summaries attached to the wrong passage. Coverage is being filled in book by book; ranges with no entry simply show no summary.

summaries.Numbers 28:9-28:15: The musaf offerings for Shabbat and for Rosh Chodesh -- two lambs, then the new month's bulls, a ram, seven lambs, and a goat sin-offering.
summaries.Numbers 7:18-7:23: The second day: Netanel of Yissachar.
summaries.II Kings 12:1-12:17: King Yehoash orders the kohanim to collect money from the people to repair the Temple.
summaries.II Kings 11:17-12:17: Yehoash is crowned king at age seven after Atalyah's death, then orders the Temple repaired with money collected from the people.
summaries.I Samuel 15:1-15:34: Shaul is sent to wipe out Amalek but spares King Agag and the best of the flocks; Shmuel rebukes him and kills Agag himself.
summaries.I Samuel 15:2-15:34: Shaul is sent to wipe out Amalek but spares King Agag and the best of the flocks; Shmuel rebukes him and kills Agag himself.
summaries.Ezekiel 36:16-36:38: God promises to sprinkle Israel with pure water, give them a new heart, and gather them back from among the nations.
summaries.Ezekiel 36:16-36:36: God promises to sprinkle Israel with pure water, give them a new heart, and gather them back from among the nations.
summaries.Ezekiel 45:16-46:18: The prince's offerings for Rosh Chodesh, the festivals, and Shabbat in the future Temple, and the rules for his own land grant.
summaries.Ezekiel 45:18-46:15: The prince's offerings for Rosh Chodesh, the festivals, and the daily Shabbat sacrifice in the future Temple.
summaries.Ezekiel 45:18-46:16: The prince's offerings for Rosh Chodesh, the festivals, and Shabbat in the future Temple, and the start of the rules for his land grant.
summaries.Malachi 3:4-3:24: The coming day of judgment, the call to bring the full tithe, and the promise that Eliyah will return before that day.
summaries.Isaiah 66:1-66:24: God's greatness beyond any house built for Him, Jerusalem's future joy, and all flesh coming to worship before Him every Shabbat and Rosh Chodesh.
summaries.I Samuel 20:18-20:42: Yonatan tests Shaul's intentions toward David with the arrow signal, then the two part in tears.
summaries.Hosea 14:2-14:10: 'Return, Israel, to the LORD your God' -- the call to repent and the promise of healing.
summaries.Joel 2:15-2:27: A call to gather in fasting and prayer, with the promise to restore all that the locust devoured.
summaries.Micah 7:18-7:20: 'Who is a God like You, who pardons iniquity' -- the closing verses also recited at Tashlich.
summaries.Jeremiah 4:1-4:2: 'If you return, Israel, return to Me' -- a call to return in truth, justice, and righteousness.
summaries.Ezekiel 20:2-20:20: God recounts Israel's rebellion in Egypt and the wilderness, yet preserves them for His name's sake and gives them Shabbat as a sign.
summaries.Isaiah 66:1-66:1: 'The heavens are My throne' -- a verse appended, per Sefardi custom, so the haftarah ends on God's greatness rather than the preceding rebuke.
summaries.Isaiah 66:23-66:23: 'All flesh shall come to worship before Me' -- this hopeful verse is repeated after the harsh closing verse (66:24) so the reading ends on a positive note.
summaries.Genesis 1:1-2:3: Creation, day by day, ending with the first Shabbat.
summaries.Genesis 2:4-2:19: Adam is formed from the dust and placed in Eden, with one tree forbidden.
summaries.Genesis 2:20-3:21: Chava is formed, the snake persuades her, and the two are found out.
summaries.Genesis 3:22-4:18: Expelled from Eden; Kayin kills Hevel and is sent to wander.
summaries.Genesis 4:19-4:22: Lemech's two wives and the sons who founded herding, music and metalwork.
summaries.Genesis 4:23-5:24: Lemech's boast, the birth of Shet, and ten generations down to Chanoch.
summaries.Genesis 5:25-6:8: Noach is born; the world fills with corruption and God resolves to end it.
summaries.Genesis 6:5-6:8: The earth is corrupt, God regrets making it, and Noach alone finds favour.
summaries.Genesis 6:9-6:22: Noach is told to build the ark, down to its measurements.
summaries.Genesis 7:1-7:16: The animals board two by two and the rain begins.
summaries.Genesis 7:17-8:14: The flood covers the earth, then recedes; the raven and the dove.
summaries.Genesis 8:15-9:7: Leaving the ark: Noach's offering, and the command to be fruitful.
summaries.Genesis 9:8-9:17: The rainbow, given as the sign that the flood will never return.
summaries.Genesis 9:18-10:32: Noach's drunkenness and Cham's disgrace, then the seventy nations.
summaries.Genesis 11:1-11:32: The Tower of Bavel and the scattering; Shem's line down to Avram.
summaries.Genesis 11:29-11:32: Avram and Nachor marry; Terach leaves Ur for Charan and dies there.
summaries.Genesis 12:1-12:13: 'Lech lecha' — Avram leaves for Canaan, then famine drives him to Egypt.
summaries.Genesis 12:14-13:4: Sarai is taken to Pharaoh's house; plagues follow and Avram is sent away.
summaries.Genesis 13:5-13:18: Avram and Lot part ways, and the land is promised to Avram.
summaries.Genesis 14:1-14:20: The war of four kings against five; Lot is captured and rescued.
summaries.Genesis 14:21-15:6: Avram refuses Sodom's spoils; God promises offspring as many as the stars.
summaries.Genesis 15:7-17:6: The Covenant Between the Parts, Hagar and Yishmael, and the command of milah.
summaries.Genesis 17:7-17:27: The covenant of circumcision; Sarai becomes Sarah and Avraham circumcises his household.
summaries.Genesis 17:24-17:27: Avraham at ninety-nine and Yishmael at thirteen are circumcised, with every man of the household.
summaries.Genesis 18:1-18:14: Three visitors at the tent; Sarah laughs at the promise of a son.
summaries.Genesis 18:15-18:33: Avraham argues with God to save Sodom for the sake of the righteous.
summaries.Genesis 19:1-19:20: The angels reach Sodom, the townspeople besiege Lot's door, and he is told to run.
summaries.Genesis 19:21-21:4: Sodom is destroyed and Lot's wife looks back; later, Yitzchak is born.
summaries.Genesis 21:5-21:21: Yitzchak is weaned; Hagar and Yishmael are sent away and saved in the desert.
summaries.Genesis 21:22-21:34: Avraham and Avimelech make a treaty over a well at Be'er Sheva.
summaries.Genesis 22:1-22:24: The binding of Yitzchak, the ram, and news of Rivka's birth.
summaries.Genesis 22:20-22:24: Nachor's children are listed, ending with the birth of Rivka.
summaries.Genesis 23:1-23:16: Sarah dies and Avraham buys the cave of Machpelah as a burial plot.
summaries.Genesis 23:17-24:9: The field is deeded over; Avraham makes his servant swear to find Yitzchak a wife.
summaries.Genesis 24:10-24:26: At the well, Rivka waters ten camels and the sign is answered.
summaries.Genesis 24:27-24:52: The servant retells the whole story to Lavan and Betuel.
summaries.Genesis 24:53-24:67: Rivka agrees to go, and meets Yitzchak in the field at dusk.
summaries.Genesis 25:1-25:11: Avraham marries Keturah, dies at 175, and is buried by his sons.
summaries.Genesis 25:12-25:18: Yishmael's twelve sons and the territory they settled.
summaries.Genesis 25:16-25:18: Yishmael's twelve chieftains, his death, and where his descendants dwelt.
summaries.Genesis 25:19-26:5: The twins struggle in the womb; Esav sells his birthright for stew.
summaries.Genesis 26:6-26:12: Yitzchak in Gerar calls Rivka his sister, sows, and reaps a hundredfold.
summaries.Genesis 26:13-26:22: Yitzchak grows rich and the Philistines stop up his wells one by one.
summaries.Genesis 26:23-26:29: God appears at Be'er Sheva; Avimelech comes seeking a pact.
summaries.Genesis 26:30-27:27: Esav goes out to hunt and Yaakov, disguised, comes in for the blessing.
summaries.Genesis 27:28-28:4: The blessing is given, Esav cries out, and Yaakov is sent away to Lavan.
summaries.Genesis 28:5-28:9: Yaakov sets off for Padan Aram; Esav marries a daughter of Yishmael.
summaries.Genesis 28:7-28:9: Yaakov obeys and goes; Esav, seeing this, marries Machalat.
summaries.Genesis 28:10-28:22: The ladder dream at Beit El and the vow Yaakov makes there.
summaries.Genesis 29:1-29:17: Yaakov rolls the stone off the well and meets Rachel.
summaries.Genesis 29:18-30:13: Seven years for Rachel, Leah substituted, and the first sons are born.
summaries.Genesis 30:14-30:27: The mandrakes, more sons, and at last the birth of Yosef.
summaries.Genesis 30:28-31:16: The speckled and spotted flocks; Yaakov prospers and is told to go home.
summaries.Genesis 31:17-31:42: Yaakov flees; Rachel hides her father's idols and Lavan searches in vain.
summaries.Genesis 31:43-32:3: A treaty heap is raised as a boundary; angels meet Yaakov on the way.
summaries.Genesis 32:1-32:3: Lavan turns for home, and Yaakov encounters angels at Machanayim.
summaries.Genesis 32:4-32:13: Messengers to Esav come back with alarming news; Yaakov prays.
summaries.Genesis 32:14-32:30: A vast gift is sent ahead; Yaakov wrestles till dawn and is renamed Yisrael.
summaries.Genesis 32:31-33:5: Limping from Peniel, Yaakov finally faces Esav, who runs to embrace him.
summaries.Genesis 33:6-33:20: The families are presented, the brothers part, and Yaakov settles near Shechem.
summaries.Genesis 34:1-35:11: Dina is violated, Shimon and Levi destroy the city, and Yaakov returns to Beit El.
summaries.Genesis 35:12-36:19: Rachel dies giving birth to Binyamin; Yitzchak dies; Esav's line begins.
summaries.Genesis 36:20-36:43: The clans of Seir and the kings who reigned in Edom.
summaries.Genesis 36:40-36:43: The chiefs descended from Esav, listed by name and place.
summaries.Genesis 37:1-37:11: Yosef's coat and his two dreams turn his brothers against him.
summaries.Genesis 37:12-37:22: Sent to find his brothers, Yosef is spotted and a plot is hatched.
summaries.Genesis 37:23-37:36: Stripped, thrown in the pit and sold; the coat is dipped in blood.
summaries.Genesis 38:1-38:30: Yehuda and Tamar, and the birth of Peretz and Zerach.
summaries.Genesis 39:1-39:6: Yosef prospers in Potifar's house and is put in charge of everything.
summaries.Genesis 39:7-39:23: Potifar's wife accuses Yosef, and he lands in prison.
summaries.Genesis 40:1-40:23: The cupbearer and the baker dream, and Yosef reads both dreams.
summaries.Genesis 40:20-40:23: At Pharaoh's birthday feast the cupbearer is restored — and forgets Yosef.
summaries.Genesis 41:1-41:14: Pharaoh dreams of cows and ears of grain; Yosef is rushed from the pit.
summaries.Genesis 41:15-41:38: Yosef reads the dreams as seven years of plenty and seven of famine.
summaries.Genesis 41:39-41:52: Yosef is made viceroy over Egypt; Menashe and Efraim are born.
summaries.Genesis 41:53-42:18: Famine bites; the brothers come down and Yosef accuses them of spying.
summaries.Genesis 42:19-43:15: Shimon is held, the money reappears in the sacks, and Binyamin is sent.
summaries.Genesis 43:16-43:29: The brothers are brought to Yosef's house, and he sees Binyamin.
summaries.Genesis 43:30-44:17: Yosef weeps, the feast is held, and his goblet is planted in Binyamin's sack.
summaries.Genesis 44:14-44:17: The brothers fall before Yosef, who demands only the one with the goblet.
summaries.Genesis 44:18-44:30: Yehuda steps forward and pleads for Binyamin.
summaries.Genesis 44:31-45:7: Yehuda offers himself as a slave, and Yosef can hold back no longer.
summaries.Genesis 45:8-45:18: Yosef sends for his father; Pharaoh hears and welcomes the family.
summaries.Genesis 45:19-45:27: Wagons are sent, and Yaakov's spirit revives when he hears Yosef lives.
summaries.Genesis 45:28-46:27: Yaakov travels down to Egypt; the seventy of his household are named.
summaries.Genesis 46:28-47:10: Father and son reunite in Goshen, and Yaakov blesses Pharaoh.
summaries.Genesis 47:11-47:27: As the famine deepens, Yosef gathers all Egypt's land for Pharaoh.
summaries.Genesis 47:25-47:27: Egypt becomes Pharaoh's, at a fifth; Israel settles and multiplies in Goshen.
summaries.Genesis 47:28-48:9: Yaakov asks not to be buried in Egypt; Yosef brings his two sons.
summaries.Genesis 48:10-48:16: Yaakov claims Efraim and Menashe as his own and blesses them.
summaries.Genesis 48:17-48:22: Yaakov crosses his hands, putting the younger before the elder.
summaries.Genesis 49:1-49:18: Yaakov gathers his sons and blesses them, from Reuven through Dan.
summaries.Genesis 49:19-49:26: The blessings continue, from Gad through to Yosef.
summaries.Genesis 49:27-50:20: Yaakov dies and is carried to Machpelah; the brothers fear Yosef's revenge.
summaries.Genesis 50:21-50:26: Yosef reassures his brothers, and makes them swear to carry his bones up.
summaries.Genesis 50:23-50:26: Yosef lives to see Efraim's great-grandchildren and dies at a hundred and ten.
summaries.Exodus 1:1-1:17: The family that came down to Egypt multiplies, a new king enslaves them, and the midwives refuse to kill.
summaries.Exodus 1:18-2:10: Boys are thrown into the Nile; Moshe is hidden, then drawn out of the water.
summaries.Exodus 2:11-2:25: Moshe kills an Egyptian, flees to Midian and marries Tzipora.
summaries.Exodus 3:1-3:15: The bush burns without being consumed, and God gives Moshe His name.
summaries.Exodus 3:16-4:17: The mission is spelled out, three signs are given, and Moshe keeps refusing until Aharon is appointed.
summaries.Exodus 4:18-4:31: Moshe heads back to Egypt; the strange night encounter on the way; the people believe.
summaries.Exodus 5:1-6:1: 'Let My people go' — Pharaoh's answer is to stop supplying straw.
summaries.Exodus 5:22-6:1: Moshe asks why things have only got worse; God promises Pharaoh will drive them out.
summaries.Exodus 6:2-6:13: The four expressions of redemption — but the people, crushed by labour, don't listen.
summaries.Exodus 6:14-6:28: The line of Reuven, Shimon and Levi, down to Moshe and Aharon.
summaries.Exodus 6:29-7:7: Moshe pleads that he can't speak; Aharon is made his mouthpiece.
summaries.Exodus 7:8-8:6: The staff becomes a serpent; then blood, then frogs.
summaries.Exodus 8:7-8:18: The frogs die off, lice come, and the magicians admit defeat.
summaries.Exodus 8:19-9:16: Wild beasts, pestilence and boils; Pharaoh hardens each time.
summaries.Exodus 9:17-9:35: Hail and fire together; Pharaoh confesses, then takes it back.
summaries.Exodus 9:33-9:35: The hail stops, and Pharaoh hardens his heart once again.
summaries.Exodus 10:1-10:11: Locusts are threatened, and Pharaoh's own servants beg him to give in.
summaries.Exodus 10:12-10:23: Locusts strip the land bare, then darkness so thick no one moves.
summaries.Exodus 10:24-11:3: Pharaoh banishes Moshe from his presence; the final plague is announced.
summaries.Exodus 11:4-12:20: Death of the firstborn foretold; the Pesach lamb and the laws of matzah.
summaries.Exodus 12:21-12:28: The elders are told to take the lamb and mark the doorposts with blood.
summaries.Exodus 12:29-12:51: At midnight the firstborn die and Israel is driven out of Egypt.
summaries.Exodus 13:1-13:16: The firstborn are consecrated; tefillin, and what to tell your child.
summaries.Exodus 13:14-13:16: 'When your son asks you tomorrow' — the sign on your arm and between your eyes.
summaries.Exodus 13:17-14:8: The roundabout route, Yosef's bones, the pillar of cloud — and Pharaoh gives chase.
summaries.Exodus 14:9-14:14: Trapped against the sea, the people panic; 'God will fight for you.'
summaries.Exodus 14:15-14:25: The sea splits and Israel walks through on dry land.
summaries.Exodus 14:26-15:26: The waters return, and Israel sings the Song of the Sea.
summaries.Exodus 15:27-16:10: Elim's twelve springs, then hunger in the wilderness.
summaries.Exodus 16:11-16:36: Quail and manna, the double portion before Shabbat, and the jar kept as a memorial.
summaries.Exodus 17:1-17:16: Water from the rock at Massah and Merivah, then Amalek attacks.
summaries.Exodus 17:14-17:16: Write it as a memorial: the war against Amalek in every generation.
summaries.Exodus 18:1-18:12: Yitro arrives with Tzipora and the sons, and rejoices at all he hears.
summaries.Exodus 18:13-18:23: Yitro watches Moshe judge alone all day and tells him it cannot go on.
summaries.Exodus 18:24-18:27: Moshe appoints judges over thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens.
summaries.Exodus 19:1-19:6: Israel camps at Sinai and is offered the covenant: a kingdom of priests.
summaries.Exodus 19:7-19:19: Three days of preparation; the mountain smokes and the shofar grows louder.
summaries.Exodus 19:20-20:14: The Ten Commandments, spoken from the mountain.
summaries.Exodus 20:15-20:23: The people recoil and ask Moshe to speak instead; the altar of earth.
summaries.Exodus 20:19-20:23: No gods of silver or gold; an altar of earth, with no hewn stone and no steps.
summaries.Exodus 21:1-21:19: Civil law begins: the Hebrew servant, capital cases, and injury.
summaries.Exodus 21:20-22:3: The goring ox, the open pit, and the thief.
summaries.Exodus 22:4-22:26: Damage by grazing and by fire; the four types of guardian; lending without interest.
summaries.Exodus 22:27-23:5: First fruits; no false report; even your enemy's fallen donkey gets your help.
summaries.Exodus 23:6-23:19: Justice for the poor, the seventh year, Shabbat, and the three pilgrimage festivals.
summaries.Exodus 23:20-23:25: An angel will lead the way — do not rebel against him or serve their gods.
summaries.Exodus 23:26-24:18: The land promised, the covenant sealed with blood, and Moshe enters the cloud.
summaries.Exodus 24:15-24:18: The cloud covers the mountain and Moshe goes up for forty days and nights.
summaries.Exodus 25:1-25:16: The call for donations, the list of materials, and the ark.
summaries.Exodus 25:17-25:40: The kaporet and cherubim, the table, and the menorah beaten from one piece.
summaries.Exodus 26:1-26:14: The tapestries and the coverings of the Mishkan.
summaries.Exodus 26:15-26:30: The standing boards and their silver sockets.
summaries.Exodus 26:31-26:37: The parochet dividing the Holy from the Holy of Holies, and the entrance screen.
summaries.Exodus 27:1-27:8: The copper altar, hollow, with its horns and its poles.
summaries.Exodus 27:9-27:19: The courtyard: its hangings, pillars, sockets and pegs.
summaries.Exodus 27:17-27:19: The courtyard pillars banded in silver, and every peg of copper.
summaries.Exodus 27:20-28:12: Oil for the lamp, and the priestly garments down to the ephod's shoulder stones.
summaries.Exodus 28:13-28:30: The choshen with its twelve engraved stones, and the Urim and Tumim.
summaries.Exodus 28:31-28:43: The robe hung with bells, the golden tzitz, and the tunics.
summaries.Exodus 29:1-29:18: The seven-day inauguration begins: the bull and the first ram.
summaries.Exodus 29:19-29:37: The ram of inauguration, with blood placed on ear, thumb and toe.
summaries.Exodus 29:38-29:46: The daily tamid, morning and afternoon; God will dwell among them.
summaries.Exodus 30:1-30:10: The golden incense altar and its yearly atonement.
summaries.Exodus 30:8-30:10: Incense morning and evening, and blood on the altar's horns once a year.
summaries.Exodus 30:11-31:17: The half-shekel, the laver, the anointing oil and incense, Betzalel, and Shabbat.
summaries.Exodus 31:18-33:11: The tablets are given, the golden calf is made, and the tablets are smashed.
summaries.Exodus 33:12-33:16: Moshe insists that God's presence go with them, or they should not move at all.
summaries.Exodus 33:17-33:23: 'Show me Your glory' — Moshe is placed in the cleft of the rock.
summaries.Exodus 34:1-34:9: The second tablets, and the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy.
summaries.Exodus 34:10-34:26: The covenant renewed, with a warning against treaties and a repeat of the festivals.
summaries.Exodus 34:27-34:35: Forty days again; Moshe comes down with his face shining and wears a veil.
summaries.Exodus 34:33-34:35: The veil on Moshe's face, taken off whenever he speaks with God.
summaries.Exodus 35:1-35:20: Shabbat first, then the call for donations to the Mishkan.
summaries.Exodus 35:21-35:29: The people bring, men and women alike, freely and in abundance.
summaries.Exodus 35:30-36:7: Betzalel and Oholiav are appointed — and the people have to be told to stop giving.
summaries.Exodus 36:8-36:19: The tapestries and coverings are made.
summaries.Exodus 36:20-37:16: The boards, the parochet, the ark and the table are made.
summaries.Exodus 37:17-37:29: The menorah, the incense altar, the anointing oil and the incense are made.
summaries.Exodus 38:1-38:20: The copper altar, the laver made from the women's mirrors, and the courtyard.
summaries.Exodus 38:18-38:20: The courtyard's entrance screen, its pillars, and all its pegs.
summaries.Exodus 38:21-39:1: The full accounting of the gold, silver and copper that were used.
summaries.Exodus 39:2-39:21: The ephod and the choshen are made and fastened together.
summaries.Exodus 39:22-39:32: The robe, the tunics and the tzitz are finished, and the work is complete.
summaries.Exodus 39:33-39:43: Everything is brought to Moshe, who sees it is done as commanded and blesses them.
summaries.Exodus 40:1-40:16: The command to erect the Mishkan on the first of the first month.
summaries.Exodus 40:17-40:27: The Mishkan is raised, and the ark, table and menorah are set in place.
summaries.Exodus 40:28-40:38: The courtyard is completed and the cloud fills the Mishkan.
summaries.Exodus 40:34-40:38: The cloud covers the Tent and the glory fills it; the cloud governs every journey.
summaries.Leviticus 1:1-1:13: God calls to Moshe from the Tent; the olah from cattle and from sheep.
summaries.Leviticus 1:14-2:6: The bird offering, and the first of the flour offerings.
summaries.Leviticus 2:7-2:16: More mincha types, salt on every offering, and the first-grain offering.
summaries.Leviticus 3:1-3:17: The shelamim, and the ban on eating fat or blood.
summaries.Leviticus 4:1-4:26: Sin offerings for the anointed kohen, the whole community, and the ruler.
summaries.Leviticus 4:27-5:10: The individual's sin offering, and the sliding-scale offering.
summaries.Leviticus 5:11-5:26: The poor person's flour offering, and the guilt offering for theft and false oath.
summaries.Leviticus 5:24-5:26: Returning what was taken plus a fifth, and bringing the guilt offering.
summaries.Leviticus 6:1-6:11: Clearing the ashes, the fire that never goes out, and the mincha.
summaries.Leviticus 6:12-7:10: The kohen's own daily offering, the chatat, and the asham.
summaries.Leviticus 7:11-7:38: The thanksgiving and peace offerings, forbidden fat and blood, and the priests' portions.
summaries.Leviticus 8:1-8:13: The inauguration begins: Aharon and his sons are washed and dressed.
summaries.Leviticus 8:14-8:21: The bull and the first ram are offered.
summaries.Leviticus 8:22-8:29: The second ram, with blood placed on ear, thumb and toe.
summaries.Leviticus 8:30-8:36: The anointing, and seven days staying at the entrance of the Tent.
summaries.Leviticus 8:33-8:36: The seven days of inauguration are completed exactly as commanded.
summaries.Leviticus 9:1-9:16: The eighth day: Aharon brings his first offerings.
summaries.Leviticus 9:17-9:23: The offerings are finished and Aharon blesses the people.
summaries.Leviticus 9:24-10:11: Fire comes down; Nadav and Avihu bring strange fire and die.
summaries.Leviticus 10:12-10:15: What remains of the offerings, and who may eat it.
summaries.Leviticus 10:16-10:20: Moshe is angry that the goat was burned; Aharon's answer satisfies him.
summaries.Leviticus 11:1-11:32: Which animals, fish, birds and creeping things may be eaten.
summaries.Leviticus 11:33-11:47: Impurity conveyed by carcasses, and the call to be holy.
summaries.Leviticus 11:45-11:47: 'I am the Lord who brought you up from Egypt' — distinguishing pure from impure.
summaries.Leviticus 12:1-13:5: Purification after childbirth, then the first signs of tzaraat.
summaries.Leviticus 13:6-13:17: The kohen looks again after seven days; the case that turns entirely white.
summaries.Leviticus 13:18-13:23: Tzaraat appearing on the site of a boil.
summaries.Leviticus 13:24-13:28: Tzaraat appearing on the site of a burn.
summaries.Leviticus 13:29-13:39: Affliction of the head or beard, and the harmless white patch.
summaries.Leviticus 13:40-13:54: Baldness, the metzora's torn clothes and cry, and tzaraat in a garment.
summaries.Leviticus 13:55-13:59: Washing the garment, tearing out the spot, or burning the whole thing.
summaries.Leviticus 13:57-13:59: A garment that breaks out again is burned; the law for wool, linen and leather.
summaries.Leviticus 14:1-14:12: The metzora's purification: two birds, cedar wood, crimson thread and hyssop.
summaries.Leviticus 14:13-14:20: The offerings, and oil placed on ear, thumb and toe.
summaries.Leviticus 14:21-14:32: The same purification, scaled down for someone who cannot afford it.
summaries.Leviticus 14:33-14:53: Tzaraat in a house, and the stones that must be pulled out.
summaries.Leviticus 14:54-15:15: A summary of the tzaraat laws, then the laws of the zav.
summaries.Leviticus 15:16-15:28: Emissions, the niddah, and the zava.
summaries.Leviticus 15:29-15:33: The zava's offering, and a summary of all these laws.
summaries.Leviticus 15:31-15:33: Keeping Israel from impurity so that the Mishkan among them is not defiled.
summaries.Leviticus 16:1-16:17: After the death of Aharon's sons: the Yom Kippur service in the Holy of Holies.
summaries.Leviticus 16:18-16:24: The altar is purified, and the goat carrying the sins is sent off into the wilderness.
summaries.Leviticus 16:25-16:34: Yom Kippur is fixed as an eternal statute, once a year.
summaries.Leviticus 17:1-17:7: Slaughtering only at the Tent, and an end to offerings in the field.
summaries.Leviticus 17:8-18:5: Covering the blood; 'you shall live by them, not die by them.'
summaries.Leviticus 18:6-18:21: The forbidden relations, listed one by one.
summaries.Leviticus 18:22-18:30: Further prohibitions, and the warning that the land vomits out its inhabitants.
summaries.Leviticus 18:28-18:30: Do not defile the land as the nations before you did.
summaries.Leviticus 19:1-19:14: 'You shall be holy' — a rapid run of mitzvot, from revering parents to not cursing the deaf.
summaries.Leviticus 19:15-19:22: Honest judgement, not standing by your brother's blood, and 'love your neighbour as yourself.'
summaries.Leviticus 19:23-19:32: Orlah, not rounding the beard, tattoos, and rising before the elderly.
summaries.Leviticus 19:33-19:37: Loving the stranger, and honest weights and measures.
summaries.Leviticus 20:1-20:7: Molech, and turning to mediums and oracles.
summaries.Leviticus 20:8-20:22: The penalties attached to the forbidden relations.
summaries.Leviticus 20:23-20:27: Separating from the nations' practices, and from impure animals.
summaries.Leviticus 20:25-20:27: Distinguishing pure from impure; 'you shall be holy to Me.'
summaries.Leviticus 21:1-21:15: A kohen and contact with the dead, and whom he may marry.
summaries.Leviticus 21:16-22:16: Blemishes that disqualify a kohen from serving, and who may eat terumah.
summaries.Leviticus 22:17-22:33: Blemished animals, and not slaughtering a parent and its young on the same day.
summaries.Leviticus 23:1-23:22: Shabbat, Pesach, the omer and Shavuot — and leaving the corners for the poor.
summaries.Leviticus 23:23-23:32: Rosh Hashana's shofar blast and the afflictions of Yom Kippur.
summaries.Leviticus 23:33-23:44: Sukkot, the four species, and dwelling in booths for seven days.
summaries.Leviticus 24:1-24:23: The lamp and the showbread, then the blasphemer and his judgement.
summaries.Leviticus 24:21-24:23: One law for stranger and citizen alike; the blasphemer is taken out and stoned.
summaries.Leviticus 25:1-25:13: Shmita, given at Sinai, and the Yovel announced by the shofar.
summaries.Leviticus 25:14-25:18: Pricing land by the years remaining to Yovel, and not wronging one another.
summaries.Leviticus 25:19-25:24: The promise of the sixth year's crop; the land may not be sold in perpetuity.
summaries.Leviticus 25:25-25:28: Redeeming a field that had to be sold.
summaries.Leviticus 25:29-25:38: Houses in a walled city, the Levites' cities, and lending without interest.
summaries.Leviticus 25:39-25:46: An impoverished brother is not to be worked as a slave.
summaries.Leviticus 25:47-26:2: Redeeming one who sold himself to a stranger; no idols, and keep Shabbat.
summaries.Leviticus 25:55-26:2: 'The children of Israel are My servants' — no idols, keep Shabbat, revere the Sanctuary.
summaries.Leviticus 26:3-26:5: 'If you walk in My statutes': rain in its season and harvests that overtake each other.
summaries.Leviticus 26:6-26:9: Peace in the land, victory over enemies, and fruitfulness.
summaries.Leviticus 26:10-26:46: God will walk among them — then the Tochacha, ending with a promise to remember the covenant.
summaries.Leviticus 27:1-27:15: Vowed valuations of people and animals, and dedicating a house.
summaries.Leviticus 27:16-27:21: Dedicating a field, and what becomes of it at Yovel.
summaries.Leviticus 27:22-27:28: A purchased field, the firstborn, and things placed under cherem.
summaries.Leviticus 27:29-27:34: Tithes of the land and of the herd, and the closing verse of the book.
summaries.Leviticus 27:32-27:34: The tithe of the herd passing under the rod; these are the commandments given at Sinai.
summaries.Numbers 1:1-1:19: The census is ordered in the wilderness of Sinai, with a chieftain named for each tribe.
summaries.Numbers 1:20-1:54: Tribe by tribe, the count is given; the Levites are set apart for the Mishkan.
summaries.Numbers 2:1-2:34: The camp is arranged, three tribes to each side of the Tent.
summaries.Numbers 3:1-3:13: Aharon's sons; the Levites are taken in place of the firstborn.
summaries.Numbers 3:14-3:39: The Levite families are counted and each given its post around the Mishkan.
summaries.Numbers 3:40-3:51: The firstborn are counted, and the surplus redeemed at five shekels each.
summaries.Numbers 4:1-4:20: How the family of Kehat is to carry the holiest vessels, covered before they move.
summaries.Numbers 4:17-4:20: A warning that Kehat must not look at the holy things and die.
summaries.Numbers 4:21-4:37: The duties of Gershon, and the count of Kehat.
summaries.Numbers 4:38-4:49: The counts of Gershon and Merari, and the total of the Levite workforce.
summaries.Numbers 5:1-5:10: Sending the impure outside the camp; confession and restitution.
summaries.Numbers 5:11-6:27: The sotah, the nazir, and Birkat Kohanim.
summaries.Numbers 7:1-7:41: The wagons are given, and the first days of the chieftains' identical offerings.
summaries.Numbers 7:42-7:71: The chieftains' offerings continue, day after day, each one the same.
summaries.Numbers 7:72-7:89: The last chieftains bring their offerings, and Moshe hears the Voice from between the cherubim.
summaries.Numbers 7:87-7:89: The totals of all twelve offerings, and the Voice speaking from above the ark.
summaries.Numbers 8:1-8:14: Aharon kindles the menorah; the Levites are purified.
summaries.Numbers 8:15-8:26: The Levites begin their service, from twenty-five until fifty.
summaries.Numbers 9:1-9:14: Pesach in the wilderness, and Pesach Sheni for those who were impure.
summaries.Numbers 9:15-10:10: The cloud over the Mishkan governs every journey; the silver trumpets.
summaries.Numbers 10:11-10:34: The cloud lifts and Israel sets out for the first time, in order of march.
summaries.Numbers 10:35-11:29: 'Arise, O Lord'; the complaints, the quail, and the seventy elders.
summaries.Numbers 11:30-12:16: The plague at Kivrot HaTaavah; Miriam and Aharon speak against Moshe.
summaries.Numbers 12:14-12:16: Miriam is shut outside the camp for seven days, and the people wait for her.
summaries.Numbers 13:1-13:20: The twelve spies are named and sent, with instructions on what to look for.
summaries.Numbers 13:21-14:7: The spies return with the giant cluster and a frightening report; the people weep.
summaries.Numbers 14:8-14:25: Yehoshua and Kalev plead; God threatens to destroy the nation and Moshe intercedes.
summaries.Numbers 14:26-15:7: The decree of forty years; those who try to go up anyway are struck down.
summaries.Numbers 15:8-15:16: The wine and flour that accompany offerings; one law for the stranger.
summaries.Numbers 15:17-15:26: Challah, and the offering for an unwitting communal error.
summaries.Numbers 15:27-15:41: The individual sin offering, the man gathering wood, and the passage of tzitzit.
summaries.Numbers 15:37-15:41: The third paragraph of the Shema: tzitzit, and remembering all the commandments.
summaries.Numbers 16:1-16:13: Korach and his assembly challenge Moshe and Aharon.
summaries.Numbers 16:14-16:19: Datan and Aviram refuse to come up; the assembly gathers with their fire-pans.
summaries.Numbers 16:20-17:8: The earth swallows Korach's company; the fire-pans are beaten into altar plating.
summaries.Numbers 17:9-17:15: The plague breaks out, and Aharon runs with incense to stop it.
summaries.Numbers 17:16-17:24: Twelve staffs are placed in the Tent, and Aharon's blossoms overnight.
summaries.Numbers 17:25-18:20: The staff kept as a sign; the duties of the kohanim and the gifts they receive.
summaries.Numbers 18:21-18:32: The tithe given to the Levites, and the tithe they give from it.
summaries.Numbers 18:30-18:32: The Levites' own portion, once the best of it has been set aside.
summaries.Numbers 19:1-19:17: The red heifer, its ashes, and the water of purification.
summaries.Numbers 19:18-20:6: Sprinkling the water; Miriam dies and the well runs dry.
summaries.Numbers 20:7-20:13: Moshe strikes the rock instead of speaking to it, and is told he will not enter the land.
summaries.Numbers 20:14-20:21: Edom refuses to let Israel pass through.
summaries.Numbers 20:22-21:9: Aharon dies on Hor HaHar; the copper snake is raised on a pole.
summaries.Numbers 21:10-21:20: The journeys through Moav, and the song at the well.
summaries.Numbers 21:21-22:1: Sichon and Og are defeated and their land taken.
summaries.Numbers 21:34-22:1: Og is delivered into Israel's hand, and they camp on the plains of Moav.
summaries.Numbers 22:2-22:12: Balak sends for Bilaam, and God tells him not to go.
summaries.Numbers 22:13-22:20: A second, grander delegation; Bilaam is permitted to go.
summaries.Numbers 22:21-22:38: The donkey sees the angel and speaks; Bilaam reaches Balak.
summaries.Numbers 22:39-23:12: Seven altars are built, and Bilaam blesses instead of cursing.
summaries.Numbers 23:13-23:26: A second vantage point, and a second blessing.
summaries.Numbers 23:27-24:13: From the peak of Peor, Bilaam blesses again — 'Mah tovu'.
summaries.Numbers 24:14-25:9: Bilaam's final oracles; Baal Peor, and Pinchas halts the plague.
summaries.Numbers 25:7-25:9: Pinchas acts, and the plague that had killed twenty-four thousand stops.
summaries.Numbers 25:10-26:4: Pinchas is given the covenant of peace; a new census is ordered.
summaries.Numbers 26:5-26:51: The second census, family by family, tribe by tribe.
summaries.Numbers 26:52-27:5: Dividing the land by lot; the daughters of Tzelofchad come forward.
summaries.Numbers 27:6-27:23: Their claim is upheld; Yehoshua is appointed as Moshe's successor.
summaries.Numbers 28:1-28:15: The daily tamid, the Shabbat offering, and Rosh Chodesh.
summaries.Numbers 28:16-29:11: The festival offerings for Pesach, Shavuot, Rosh Hashana and Yom Kippur.
summaries.Numbers 29:12-30:1: The Sukkot offerings, with the bulls decreasing day by day.
summaries.Numbers 29:35-30:1: Shemini Atzeret's offering, and the close of the festival list.
summaries.Numbers 30:2-30:17: Vows and oaths, and when a father or husband may annul them.
summaries.Numbers 31:1-31:12: The war against Midian, and the spoils brought back.
summaries.Numbers 31:13-31:24: Moshe's anger at the returning army; purifying the vessels through fire.
summaries.Numbers 31:25-31:41: The spoils are counted and divided between the soldiers and the community.
summaries.Numbers 31:42-31:54: The officers find not one man missing, and bring gold as atonement.
summaries.Numbers 32:1-32:19: Reuven and Gad ask for land east of the Jordan; Moshe accuses them of repeating the spies' sin.
summaries.Numbers 32:20-32:42: They agree to cross over armed, and the eastern land is assigned.
summaries.Numbers 32:39-32:42: Machir, Yair and Novach take territory in the Gilad and rename it.
summaries.Numbers 33:1-33:10: The record of the journeys begins, from Rameses to the wilderness.
summaries.Numbers 33:11-33:49: The forty-two stations, one after another, all the way to the plains of Moav.
summaries.Numbers 33:50-34:15: Clear out the inhabitants and their idols; the borders of the land are drawn.
summaries.Numbers 34:16-34:29: The men appointed to apportion the land, one leader per tribe.
summaries.Numbers 35:1-35:8: The forty-eight Levite cities and their surrounding open land.
summaries.Numbers 35:9-35:34: The cities of refuge, and the difference between murder and manslaughter.
summaries.Numbers 36:1-36:13: The daughters of Tzelofchad must marry within their tribe, so no land moves between tribes.
summaries.Numbers 36:11-36:13: Tzelofchad's daughters marry their cousins; the closing verse of the book.
summaries.Deuteronomy 1:1-1:10: Moshe begins his final address, forty years on, at the edge of the land.
summaries.Deuteronomy 1:11-1:21: Appointing judges over the people; 'go up and take possession'.
summaries.Deuteronomy 1:22-1:38: Moshe retells the spies: the people's refusal, and the decree that followed.
summaries.Deuteronomy 1:39-2:1: The children will enter instead; the failed attempt to go up, and years of wandering.
summaries.Deuteronomy 2:2-2:30: Passing by Esav's descendants in Seir, and by Moav and Ammon, without provoking them; Sichon refuses passage.
summaries.Deuteronomy 2:31-3:14: Sichon and Og are defeated, and their land given to Reuven, Gad and half of Menashe.
summaries.Deuteronomy 3:15-3:22: The eastern tribes must cross over armed; Yehoshua is told not to fear.
summaries.Deuteronomy 3:20-3:22: Israel's brothers must be settled too; 'the Lord your God is the one who fights for you'.
summaries.Deuteronomy 3:23-4:4: Moshe pleads to be allowed in, and is refused; a warning from Baal Peor.
summaries.Deuteronomy 4:5-4:40: Guard the commandments; remember that at Chorev you saw no image, only heard a voice.
summaries.Deuteronomy 4:41-4:49: Three cities of refuge east of the Jordan; the introduction to the law.
summaries.Deuteronomy 5:1-5:18: The Ten Commandments, repeated to the generation about to enter.
summaries.Deuteronomy 5:19-6:3: The people ask Moshe to receive the rest on their behalf.
summaries.Deuteronomy 6:4-6:25: Shema Yisrael, and the answer to give a child who asks why.
summaries.Deuteronomy 7:1-7:11: The seven nations, no intermarriage, and why Israel was chosen.
summaries.Deuteronomy 7:9-7:11: God keeps covenant to a thousand generations, and repays those who hate Him.
summaries.Deuteronomy 7:12-8:10: The blessing of obedience; the land of seven species, and Birkat HaMazon.
summaries.Deuteronomy 8:11-9:3: Do not say 'my own strength made me this wealth'; crossing to face greater nations.
summaries.Deuteronomy 9:4-9:29: Not for your righteousness — the golden calf and Moshe's forty days of prayer.
summaries.Deuteronomy 10:1-10:11: The second tablets and the ark; what God asks of you.
summaries.Deuteronomy 10:12-11:9: Circumcise your heart, love the stranger, and remember what your own eyes saw.
summaries.Deuteronomy 11:10-11:21: The land that drinks rain from heaven, and the second paragraph of the Shema.
summaries.Deuteronomy 11:22-11:25: Every place your foot treads will be yours; no one will stand against you.
summaries.Deuteronomy 11:26-12:10: Blessing and curse at Gerizim and Eival; destroy the idols and their sites.
summaries.Deuteronomy 12:11-12:28: Offerings only at the chosen place; meat may be eaten anywhere, but never the blood.
summaries.Deuteronomy 12:29-13:19: The enticer, the false prophet, and the wayward city.
summaries.Deuteronomy 14:1-14:21: Not to gash yourselves in mourning; the kosher animals, birds and fish.
summaries.Deuteronomy 14:22-14:29: The second tithe, taken up to the chosen place, and the tithe for the poor.
summaries.Deuteronomy 15:1-15:18: The release of debts, the prozbul problem of the seventh year, and the Hebrew servant.
summaries.Deuteronomy 15:19-16:17: The firstborn animal, and the three pilgrimage festivals.
summaries.Deuteronomy 16:13-16:17: Sukkot, and appearing three times a year, each with a gift in hand.
summaries.Deuteronomy 16:18-17:13: Appoint judges and officers; 'justice, justice shall you pursue'.
summaries.Deuteronomy 17:14-17:20: The laws of a king, who must write himself a Torah scroll and keep it with him.
summaries.Deuteronomy 18:1-18:5: The kohanim have no portion of land; the gifts that are theirs instead.
summaries.Deuteronomy 18:6-18:13: A Levite who comes to serve; the forbidden forms of divination.
summaries.Deuteronomy 18:14-19:13: The true prophet against the false one; the cities of refuge.
summaries.Deuteronomy 19:14-20:9: Moving a boundary marker, witnesses, and who is sent home before a battle.
summaries.Deuteronomy 20:10-21:9: The laws of siege, not destroying fruit trees, and the eglah arufah.
summaries.Deuteronomy 21:7-21:9: The elders declare their hands did not shed this blood, and atonement is made.
summaries.Deuteronomy 21:10-21:21: The captive woman, the hated wife's firstborn, and the rebellious son.
summaries.Deuteronomy 21:22-22:7: Burial the same day, returning lost property, and sending away the mother bird.
summaries.Deuteronomy 22:8-23:7: A parapet on the roof, forbidden mixtures, and who may enter the congregation.
summaries.Deuteronomy 23:8-23:24: Keeping the camp holy, not returning a runaway slave, interest, and vows.
summaries.Deuteronomy 23:25-24:4: Eating from your neighbour's vineyard, and the laws of divorce.
summaries.Deuteronomy 24:5-24:13: The first year of marriage, kidnapping, tzaraat, and returning a poor man's pledge.
summaries.Deuteronomy 24:14-25:19: Paying wages on time, the wayward brother, honest weights — and remembering Amalek.
summaries.Deuteronomy 25:17-25:19: Remember what Amalek did to you on the way out of Egypt; blot out his memory.
summaries.Deuteronomy 26:1-26:11: Bringing the first fruits, and the declaration made with the basket.
summaries.Deuteronomy 26:12-26:15: The confession of the tithes in the third year.
summaries.Deuteronomy 26:16-26:19: 'Today you have affirmed' — the mutual declaration between God and Israel.
summaries.Deuteronomy 27:1-27:10: The stones plastered and inscribed, and the altar on Har Eival.
summaries.Deuteronomy 27:11-28:6: Six tribes on each mountain; the twelve curses, then the blessings.
summaries.Deuteronomy 28:7-28:69: The blessings, then the Tochacha — the long rebuke, read quickly and quietly.
summaries.Deuteronomy 29:1-29:8: Your eyes saw what happened in Egypt; keep this covenant and succeed.
summaries.Deuteronomy 29:6-29:8: Sichon and Og were defeated and their land given as an inheritance.
summaries.Deuteronomy 29:9-29:11: 'You are standing here today' — the whole nation, from woodcutter to water-drawer.
summaries.Deuteronomy 29:12-29:14: The covenant is made with those present and with those not yet born.
summaries.Deuteronomy 29:15-29:28: A warning against the one who blesses himself while going his own way.
summaries.Deuteronomy 30:1-30:6: Return, and God will gather you back from the ends of the earth.
summaries.Deuteronomy 30:7-30:10: The curses turned on your enemies; return with all your heart.
summaries.Deuteronomy 30:11-30:14: 'It is not in heaven' — the Torah is very close, in your mouth and heart.
summaries.Deuteronomy 30:15-30:20: 'I have set before you life and death' — choose life.
summaries.Deuteronomy 31:1-31:3: Moshe, a hundred and twenty, says he can no longer go out and come in.
summaries.Deuteronomy 31:4-31:6: 'Be strong and courageous' — God goes before you and will not forsake you.
summaries.Deuteronomy 31:7-31:9: Yehoshua is charged in front of everyone; the Torah is written and given to the kohanim.
summaries.Deuteronomy 31:10-31:13: Hakhel: gathering the whole nation every seven years to hear the Torah read.
summaries.Deuteronomy 31:14-31:19: Moshe and Yehoshua at the Tent; the command to write down the song.
summaries.Deuteronomy 31:20-31:24: The song as a witness; Moshe finishes writing the Torah.
summaries.Deuteronomy 31:25-31:30: The scroll placed beside the ark, and Moshe speaks the song aloud.
summaries.Deuteronomy 31:28-31:30: Assemble the elders and let heaven and earth witness; Moshe begins the song.
summaries.Deuteronomy 32:1-32:6: 'Listen, heavens' — the song opens, calling Israel ungrateful.
summaries.Deuteronomy 32:7-32:12: Remember the days of old; God found them in a desert land and bore them on eagles' wings.
summaries.Deuteronomy 32:13-32:18: Fed with the richest of the land, Yeshurun grew fat and kicked.
summaries.Deuteronomy 32:19-32:28: God hides His face; a nation without counsel.
summaries.Deuteronomy 32:29-32:39: 'See now that I am He' — there is no god beside Him.
summaries.Deuteronomy 32:40-32:43: God raises His hand in oath; the song ends by promising to avenge His servants.
summaries.Deuteronomy 32:44-32:52: The song delivered; Moshe is told to climb Har Nevo and see the land.
summaries.Deuteronomy 32:48-32:52: Go up Har Nevo, see the land from a distance, and die there as Aharon did.
summaries.Deuteronomy 33:1-33:7: Moshe's final blessing begins, with Reuven and Yehuda.
summaries.Deuteronomy 33:8-33:12: The blessings of Levi and Binyamin.
summaries.Deuteronomy 33:13-33:17: Yosef's blessing: the bounty of heaven and earth.
summaries.Deuteronomy 33:22-33:26: Dan, Naftali and Asher, and 'there is none like God, Yeshurun'.
summaries.Deuteronomy 33:27-33:29: 'The eternal God is a refuge' — Israel dwells secure and alone.
summaries.Deuteronomy 34:1-34:12: Moshe sees the whole land from Har Nevo, dies, and is buried in an unknown grave.
summaries.Exodus 35:1-35:29: Shabbat, then the call for donations — and the people bring more than enough.
summaries.Exodus 35:30-37:16: Betzalel and Oholiav appointed; the tapestries, boards, ark and table made.
summaries.Exodus 38:1-39:1: The copper altar, the laver, the courtyard, and the accounting of the metals.
summaries.Exodus 39:22-39:43: The last garments finished; everything is brought to Moshe, who blesses them.
summaries.Exodus 40:1-40:38: The Mishkan is erected on the first of the month, and the cloud fills it.
summaries.Leviticus 12:1-13:23: Purification after childbirth, and the first cases of tzaraat.
summaries.Leviticus 13:24-13:39: Tzaraat on a burn, on the head or beard, and the harmless white patch.
summaries.Leviticus 13:55-14:20: Burning the affected garment; the metzora's purification with birds and oil.
summaries.Leviticus 14:33-15:15: Tzaraat in a house, then the laws of the zav.
summaries.Leviticus 15:16-15:33: Emissions, the niddah and the zava, and the summary of these laws.
summaries.Leviticus 16:1-16:24: The Yom Kippur service, and the goat sent off into the wilderness.
summaries.Leviticus 16:25-17:7: Yom Kippur fixed as an eternal statute; slaughtering only at the Tent.
summaries.Leviticus 17:8-18:21: The blood prohibition, 'you shall live by them', and the forbidden relations.
summaries.Leviticus 18:22-19:14: The land vomits out its inhabitants; 'you shall be holy' and the mitzvot that follow.
summaries.Leviticus 19:15-19:32: 'Love your neighbour as yourself', orlah, and rising before the elderly.
summaries.Leviticus 19:33-20:7: Loving the stranger, honest measures, Molech, and mediums.
summaries.Leviticus 20:8-20:27: The penalties for forbidden relations, and separating from the nations' ways.
summaries.Leviticus 25:1-25:18: Shmita and Yovel, given at Sinai, and not wronging one another in trade.
summaries.Leviticus 25:19-25:28: The sixth year's crop, land not sold in perpetuity, and redeeming a field.
summaries.Leviticus 25:39-26:9: An impoverished brother is not a slave; no idols; the blessings of obedience.
summaries.Leviticus 27:16-27:34: Dedicating fields, the firstborn, cherem, and the tithes of land and herd.
summaries.Numbers 19:1-20:6: The red heifer and its ashes; Miriam dies and the well runs dry.
summaries.Numbers 20:7-20:21: Moshe strikes the rock; Edom refuses to let Israel pass.
summaries.Numbers 20:22-21:20: Aharon dies on Hor HaHar; the copper snake, and the song at the well.
summaries.Numbers 21:21-22:12: Sichon and Og defeated; Balak sends for Bilaam.
summaries.Numbers 22:13-22:38: A grander delegation; the donkey sees the angel and speaks.
summaries.Numbers 22:39-23:26: Seven altars twice over, and Bilaam blesses instead of cursing.
summaries.Numbers 23:27-25:9: 'Mah tovu' and the final oracles; Baal Peor, and Pinchas halts the plague.
summaries.Numbers 30:2-31:12: Vows and their annulment, then the war against Midian.
summaries.Numbers 31:13-31:54: The spoils purified, counted and divided; not one soldier is missing.
summaries.Numbers 32:20-33:49: The eastern tribes agree to cross over armed; the forty-two journeys are recorded.
summaries.Numbers 34:16-35:8: Those appointed to divide the land, and the forty-eight Levite cities.
summaries.Numbers 35:9-36:13: The cities of refuge, and the daughters of Tzelofchad marrying within their tribe.
summaries.Deuteronomy 29:9-29:28: 'You are standing here today' — the covenant made with every generation.
summaries.Deuteronomy 30:7-30:14: Return with all your heart; 'it is not in heaven'.
summaries.Deuteronomy 30:15-31:6: 'Choose life'; Moshe at a hundred and twenty says he can no longer lead.
summaries.Deuteronomy 31:7-31:13: Yehoshua is charged publicly, and Hakhel is commanded every seven years.
summaries.Deuteronomy 31:20-31:30: The song as a witness; the scroll placed beside the ark.
summaries.Exodus 32:11-32:14: Moshe pleads after the golden calf, and the decree is relented — read on fast days.
summaries.Exodus 34:1-34:3: Carve the second tablets and come up the mountain alone.
summaries.Exodus 34:4-34:10: Moshe ascends at dawn and God passes before him: the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy.
summaries.Exodus 34:1-34:10: The second tablets, and the Thirteen Attributes proclaimed on the mountain.
summaries.Exodus 33:17-33:19: 'Show me Your glory' — God agrees to let His goodness pass by.
summaries.Exodus 33:20-33:23: No one may see God's face; Moshe is hidden in the cleft of the rock.
summaries.Exodus 34:11-34:17: A warning against treaties with the inhabitants and against molten gods.
summaries.Exodus 34:18-34:26: The festivals, the firstborn, Shabbat, and the first fruits.
summaries.Numbers 7:1-7:17: The Mishkan anointed, the wagons given, and Nachshon brings the first day's offering.
summaries.Numbers 7:18-7:20: The second day: Netanel of Yissachar brings his offering.
summaries.Numbers 7:24-7:29: The third day: Eliav of Zevulun.
summaries.Numbers 7:30-7:35: The fourth day: Elitzur of Reuven.
summaries.Numbers 7:36-7:41: The fifth day: Shelumiel of Shimon.
summaries.Numbers 7:42-7:47: The sixth day: Elyasaf of Gad.
summaries.Numbers 7:48-7:53: The seventh day: Elishama of Efraim.
summaries.Numbers 7:54-8:4: The eighth day's offering, and the command to kindle the menorah.
summaries.Numbers 28:1-28:5: The daily tamid offering, morning and afternoon.
summaries.Numbers 28:1-28:3: The tamid: two lambs a day, as a regular offering.
summaries.Numbers 28:3-28:5: The lambs of the tamid and the flour and oil that go with them.
summaries.Numbers 28:6-28:10: The tamid at Sinai, and the additional offering for Shabbat.
summaries.Numbers 28:16-28:25: The Pesach offering and the seven days of matzah.
summaries.Numbers 28:19-28:25: The musaf brought on each day of Pesach.
summaries.Numbers 28:26-28:31: The Shavuot offering on the day of first fruits.
summaries.Numbers 29:1-29:6: The Rosh Hashana offering, on the day of the shofar blast.
summaries.Numbers 29:7-29:11: The Yom Kippur offering, on the day of affliction.
summaries.Numbers 29:12-29:16: The first day of Sukkot: thirteen bulls.
summaries.Numbers 29:17-29:19: The second day of Sukkot: twelve bulls.
summaries.Numbers 29:20-29:22: The third day of Sukkot: eleven bulls.
summaries.Numbers 29:23-29:25: The fourth day of Sukkot: ten bulls.
summaries.Numbers 29:26-29:28: The fifth day of Sukkot: nine bulls.
summaries.Numbers 29:29-29:31: The sixth day of Sukkot: eight bulls.
summaries.Numbers 29:32-29:34: The seventh day of Sukkot: seven bulls.
summaries.Numbers 29:35-29:37: Shemini Atzeret: a single bull, and a day of assembly.
summaries.Numbers 29:17-29:22: The second and third days of Sukkot, twelve bulls then eleven.
summaries.Numbers 29:20-29:25: The third and fourth days of Sukkot, eleven bulls then ten.
summaries.Numbers 29:23-29:28: The fourth and fifth days of Sukkot, ten bulls then nine.
summaries.Numbers 29:26-29:31: The fifth and sixth days of Sukkot, nine bulls then eight.
summaries.Numbers 29:29-29:34: The sixth and seventh days of Sukkot, eight bulls then seven.
summaries.Numbers 9:1-9:5: The Pesach offering brought in the wilderness, a year after leaving Egypt.
summaries.Numbers 9:6-9:8: Men who were impure ask why they should lose out; Moshe waits for an answer.
summaries.Numbers 9:9-9:14: Pesach Sheni, a second chance a month later.
summaries.Numbers 19:1-19:22: The red heifer, its ashes, and the water that purifies — read as Parshat Parah.
summaries.Exodus 30:11-30:16: The half-shekel given by rich and poor alike — read as Parshat Shekalim.
summaries.Exodus 12:1-12:20: This month shall be first: the Pesach lamb and the laws of matzah — Parshat HaChodesh.
summaries.Exodus 12:21-12:24: The elders are told to take the lamb and mark the doorposts.
summaries.Exodus 12:25-12:28: What to answer your children about this service.
summaries.Exodus 12:29-12:36: At midnight the firstborn die, and Egypt urges Israel out.
summaries.Exodus 12:37-12:42: The departure from Rameses, and the night of watching.
summaries.Exodus 12:43-12:51: Who may eat the Pesach offering.
summaries.Exodus 13:1-13:4: The firstborn are consecrated; remember this day in the month of Aviv.
summaries.Exodus 13:5-13:10: Eating matzah for seven days, and the sign upon your hand.
summaries.Exodus 13:11-13:16: Redeeming the firstborn, and telling your son why.
summaries.Exodus 13:17-13:22: The roundabout route, Yosef's bones, and the pillar of cloud and fire.
summaries.Exodus 14:1-14:8: Israel turns back toward the sea, and Pharaoh sets out after them.
summaries.Exodus 17:8-17:10: Amalek attacks; Yehoshua goes out to fight.
summaries.Exodus 17:11-17:13: Moshe's hands are held up, and Amalek is defeated — read on Purim.
summaries.Exodus 19:7-19:13: The people accept the covenant; boundaries are set around the mountain.
summaries.Exodus 19:14-19:19: Three days of preparation; the mountain smokes and the shofar sounds.
summaries.Exodus 22:24-22:26: Lending without interest, and returning a poor man's garment before nightfall.
summaries.Leviticus 22:26-23:3: An animal must be eight days old; Shabbat heads the list of appointed times.
summaries.Leviticus 22:26-22:33: An animal may be offered from the eighth day; not slaughtering a parent and its young together.
summaries.Leviticus 22:26-23:8: From the eighth day; Shabbat, Pesach and the seven days of matzah.
summaries.Leviticus 23:1-23:3: The appointed times begin with Shabbat.
summaries.Leviticus 23:4-23:8: Pesach and the seven days of matzah.
summaries.Leviticus 23:4-23:14: Pesach, matzah, and the omer brought on the day after the festival.
summaries.Leviticus 23:9-23:14: The omer waved, and no new grain eaten until it is brought.
summaries.Leviticus 23:15-23:22: Counting fifty days to Shavuot, and leaving the corners for the poor.
summaries.Leviticus 23:15-23:44: From the omer count through Rosh Hashana, Yom Kippur and Sukkot.
summaries.Leviticus 16:1-16:6: After the death of Aharon's sons, the Yom Kippur service is set out.
summaries.Leviticus 16:7-16:11: The two goats, and the lots cast over them.
summaries.Leviticus 16:12-16:17: The incense taken within the curtain, and atonement for the Sanctuary.
summaries.Leviticus 16:25-16:30: 'On this day atonement shall be made for you' — a Shabbat of complete rest.
summaries.Leviticus 16:31-16:34: The day fixed as an eternal statute, once a year.
summaries.Genesis 21:1-21:4: Sarah conceives and Yitzchak is born, and circumcised at eight days.
summaries.Genesis 21:5-21:8: Avraham is a hundred; Sarah laughs, and Yitzchak is weaned.
summaries.Genesis 21:9-21:12: Sarah demands that Hagar and her son be sent away.
summaries.Genesis 21:13-21:17: Hagar wanders in the wilderness; God hears the boy's cry.
summaries.Genesis 21:18-21:21: A well appears, and Yishmael grows up in the wilderness.
summaries.Genesis 21:22-21:27: Avimelech comes to Avraham seeking an oath of good faith.
summaries.Genesis 21:28-21:34: Seven ewes mark the well at Be'er Sheva.
summaries.Genesis 22:1-22:3: 'Take your son' — Avraham rises early and saddles his donkey.
summaries.Genesis 22:4-22:8: On the third day they go on alone; 'God will show us the lamb'.
summaries.Genesis 22:9-22:14: The knife is raised, the angel calls out, and a ram is offered instead.
summaries.Genesis 22:15-22:19: The second call from heaven, and the promise of countless offspring.
summaries.Deuteronomy 15:19-15:23: The firstborn of the herd, offered at the chosen place.
summaries.Deuteronomy 16:1-16:3: Guard the month of Aviv and bring the Pesach offering.
summaries.Deuteronomy 16:4-16:8: Seven days of matzah, and the closing assembly.
summaries.Deuteronomy 16:9-16:12: Counting seven weeks, and rejoicing on Shavuot with everyone in your household.
summaries.Deuteronomy 4:25-4:29: A warning of exile, and the promise that seeking Him there will find Him.
summaries.Deuteronomy 4:30-4:35: In your distress you will return; nothing like this has ever happened.
summaries.Deuteronomy 4:36-4:40: He let you hear His voice from the fire, to teach you.
summaries.Deuteronomy 7:12-7:21: The blessing for keeping the laws, and no fear of the nations.
summaries.Deuteronomy 7:22-8:3: Driving them out little by little; man does not live by bread alone.
summaries.Deuteronomy 8:4-8:18: Forty years of clothes that did not wear out; do not credit your own strength.
summaries.Deuteronomy 33:27-34:12: 'The eternal God is a refuge'; Moshe sees the land, dies, and is mourned.
summaries.Isaiah 42:5-43:10: The God who created the heavens calls His servant to be a light to the nations.
summaries.Isaiah 54:1-55:5: 'The waters of Noach' — a promise that God's kindness will never depart.
summaries.Isaiah 40:27-41:16: Those who hope in God renew their strength; He calls Avraham His friend.
summaries.II Kings 4:1-4:37: Elisha and the widow's oil, then the Shunamite woman's son restored to life.
summaries.I Kings 1:1-1:31: David is old; Adoniyahu seizes the throne and Batsheva secures it for Shlomo.
summaries.Malachi 1:1-2:7: 'I loved Yaakov and hated Esav'; the priests are rebuked for blemished offerings.
summaries.Hosea 12:13-14:10: Yaakov fled to the field of Aram; Ephraim's guilt, and a call to return.
summaries.Obadiah 1:1-1:21: The whole book: Edom's downfall for standing by while Yaakov was plundered.
summaries.Amos 2:6-3:8: 'They sold the righteous for silver' — the prophet's charge against Israel.
summaries.I Kings 3:15-4:1: Shlomo wakes from his dream and judges between the two mothers.
summaries.Ezekiel 37:15-37:28: The two sticks joined into one: Yosef and Yehuda reunited.
summaries.I Kings 2:1-2:12: David's final charge to Shlomo, and his death after forty years.
summaries.Isaiah 27:6-28:13: Yaakov will take root; a warning to the drunkards of Ephraim.
summaries.Isaiah 29:22-29:23: 'Yaakov shall not now be ashamed' — the closing verses of the haftarah.
summaries.Ezekiel 28:25-29:21: Egypt as the great crocodile of the Nile, and its coming humbling.
summaries.Jeremiah 46:13-46:28: Nevuchadnetzar will strike Egypt; 'do not fear, My servant Yaakov'.
summaries.Judges 4:4-5:31: Devorah and Barak defeat Sisera, Yael drives in the tent peg, and Devorah sings.
summaries.Isaiah 6:1-7:6: Yeshayahu's vision of the throne, the seraphim, and the coal touched to his lips.
summaries.Isaiah 9:5-9:6: 'For a child has been born to us' — the closing verses of the haftarah.
summaries.Jeremiah 34:8-34:22: The covenant to free the Hebrew slaves is broken, and the freedom is revoked.
summaries.Jeremiah 33:25-33:26: 'If not for My covenant with day and night' — the closing verses.
summaries.I Kings 5:26-6:13: Shlomo begins to build the Temple, in the four hundred and eightieth year.
summaries.Ezekiel 43:10-43:27: The measurements of the altar in the future Temple, and its seven-day dedication.
summaries.I Kings 18:1-18:39: Eliyahu at Mount Carmel: the contest with the prophets of Baal.
summaries.I Kings 7:40-7:50: The bronze and gold vessels Chiram made for the Temple.
summaries.I Kings 7:51-8:21: The Temple finished; the ark brought in and the cloud fills the House.
summaries.Isaiah 43:21-44:23: 'You did not call upon Me' — and the mockery of those who carve idols.
summaries.Jeremiah 7:21-8:3: 'I did not speak to your fathers about offerings' — obedience before sacrifice.
summaries.Jeremiah 9:22-9:23: 'Let the wise not glory in his wisdom' — the closing verses.
summaries.II Samuel 6:1-7:17: The ark is brought up to the City of David, Uzzah is struck down, and David dances before it.
summaries.II Kings 4:42-5:19: The loaves that fed a hundred, and Naaman cured of tzaraat in the Jordan.
summaries.II Kings 7:3-7:20: Four men with tzaraat find the Aramean camp abandoned and end the famine.
summaries.Amos 9:7-9:15: 'Are you not like the Ethiopians to Me?' — and the promise to rebuild the fallen booth.
summaries.Ezekiel 22:1-22:19: The bloody city arraigned, offence by offence.
summaries.Ezekiel 44:15-44:31: The duties of the priests: whom they may marry, and what they may eat.
summaries.Jeremiah 32:6-32:27: Yirmiyahu buys a field in Anatot as the Babylonians besiege the city.
summaries.Jeremiah 16:19-17:14: 'Cursed is the one who trusts in man' — and blessed is the one who trusts in God.
summaries.Hosea 2:1-2:22: Israel as the unfaithful wife, betrothed again forever in righteousness.
summaries.Judges 13:2-13:25: The angel appears to Manoach's wife and announces the birth of a nazir: Shimshon.
summaries.Zechariah 2:14-4:7: The vision of the menorah: 'not by might, nor by power, but by My spirit'.
summaries.Joshua 2:1-2:24: The two spies at Rachav's house in Jericho, and the crimson cord.
summaries.I Samuel 11:14-12:22: Shmuel's farewell: 'whose ox have I taken?' — he has taken nothing from anyone.
summaries.Judges 11:1-11:33: Yiftach, driven out by his brothers, is called back to lead against Ammon.
summaries.Micah 5:6-6:8: 'What does the Lord require of you' — justice, kindness, and walking humbly.
summaries.I Kings 18:46-19:21: Eliyahu flees to Chorev and hears the still, small voice.
summaries.Jeremiah 1:1-2:3: Yirmiyahu is appointed as a prophet to the nations, though he says he is only a boy.
summaries.Jeremiah 2:4-2:28: 'They went after emptiness and became empty' — the charge against the fathers.
summaries.Jeremiah 3:4-3:4: 'Will you not from this time call to Me: my Father' — the closing verse.
summaries.Isaiah 1:1-1:27: 'Chazon Yeshayahu' — the vision read before Tisha B'Av; Zion redeemed through justice.
summaries.Isaiah 40:1-40:26: 'Nachamu, nachamu' — comfort My people, the first of the haftarot of consolation.
summaries.Isaiah 49:14-51:3: 'Zion said, the Lord has forsaken me' — and the answer that a mother cannot forget her child.
summaries.Isaiah 54:11-55:5: 'Storm-tossed one, not comforted' — the city rebuilt in precious stones, and the enduring kindnesses of David.
summaries.Isaiah 51:12-52:12: 'I, I am the one who comforts you'; awake, awake, put on your strength.
summaries.Isaiah 54:1-54:10: 'Sing, barren one' — the mountains may move, but God's kindness will not.
summaries.Isaiah 60:1-60:22: 'Arise, shine, for your light has come' — the nations stream to Zion.
summaries.Isaiah 61:10-63:9: 'I will greatly rejoice' — the last of the seven haftarot of consolation.
summaries.Isaiah 55:6-56:8: 'Seek the Lord while He may be found' — read on the fast, and for the stranger who joins.
summaries.II Samuel 22:1-22:51: David's song of deliverance, sung on the day God saved him from all his enemies.
summaries.Joshua 1:1-1:18: After Moshe's death, Yehoshua is told to be strong and to cross the Jordan.
